lesson.text: Quick memory: what three questions check a news story? (Who made it, when, and does anyone else say so?) Today: scams, fake news, privacy and passwords.
Scams offer free things if you give a password or pay first. Phishing messages look real and rush you to a link. Never log in from a link in a message: close it, tell, report.
Your school, your address, photos of you and your password stay private. What you post can be copied and stay for a long time: think before you post.
A picture can be changed in seconds. Before you share a story or a photo: who made it, when, and do trusted sources agree?
Passwords: long, never your name, never shared, not even with a friend. This game makes a guesser wait after 5 wrong tries in 15 minutes.
In a group chat that is unkind to someone: don't join in, stand by them, report it and tell a trusted adult.
Try it in the world: open Online City on the play tablet, on the Big track.

exercises.hint: Real games never ask for your password.

"Your account closes today! Log in at this link." You...
choices: don't click: open the game yourself
exercises.hint: Messages that rush you are often tricks.

exercises.prompt: Once you post a photo, it is always gone the next day.
Before sharing a story: put the checks in order.
A request: "I'm 12 too, add me!" You've never met. You...
choices: don't accept: check with a grown-up

items: pay first and win a phone
a game's settings page you opened yourself
exercises.explain: Paying first and giving passwords are scams.

exercises.prompt: A group chat laughs at a friend's video. You...
choices: don't join in, support them, report, tell
exercises.explain: Don't join in: support, report, tell.

exercises.prompt: This game's password can be your name with numbers.
exercises.explain: False: never your name, even with numbers.

exercises.prompt: An hour before bed, it's best to...
choices: put screens away and wind down
